task_row_model.query: In the described randomized trial, what was the planned sample size and allocation ratio, what was the primary outcome and its measurement timepoint, and which statistical test and significance threshold would be used for the primary analysis?

documents.content: Methods (excerpt). The trial was designed as a parallel-group randomized study enrolling 240 adult participants, allocated 1:1 to intervention or control. Eligibility criteria focused on adults aged 40–75 with untreated stage 1 hypertension. Sample size calculations assumed 80% power to detect a clinically meaningful difference and accounted for a 10% dropout rate; randomization used permuted blocks stratified by site. Recruitment timelines and consent procedures are described elsewhere. This methodological summary situates the sample size and allocation but omits outcome definitions, which appear in the protocol section.
documents.reasoning_trace: Contains the planned sample size (240) and allocation ratio (1:1); indicates power and dropout assumption (supporting design).

documents.content: Protocol summary. The primary outcome is change in clinic systolic blood pressure from baseline to 12 weeks. Blood pressure is measured at each visit as the average of three seated readings taken five minutes apart using an automated validated device; baseline and 12-week clinic averages will be compared. Secondary outcomes include diastolic pressure, adherence, and patient-reported side effects. The protocol includes visit schedules, staff training for measurement standardization, and prespecified handling of missing readings. Background commentary and secondary endpoint definitions occupy the remainder of this section.
documents.reasoning_trace: Defines the primary outcome (change in clinic systolic BP), measurement method (average of three seated readings) and timepoint (12 weeks).

documents.content: Statistical analysis plan (SAP) excerpt. The primary analysis will use analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) to compare 12-week systolic blood pressure between groups, adjusting for baseline systolic BP and site. The primary hypothesis will be tested two-sided at alpha = 0.05. Analyses will follow the intention-to-treat principle with multiple imputation for missing primary outcome data; per-protocol sensitivity analyses are also described. The SAP details model diagnostics, covariate coding, and plans for subgroup tests, which are exploratory and not multiplicity-adjusted.
documents.reasoning_trace: Specifies the primary statistical method (ANCOVA with baseline adjustment), the two-sided alpha = 0.05 threshold, and ITT analysis approach.

documents.content: Background note (informal). Hypertension trials historically shifted measurement techniques from mercury sphygmomanometers to automated devices, and earlier large trials influenced sample size heuristics. Commentators have speculated about longer follow-up and ambulatory monitoring but this trial focuses on clinic measurements. The note recounts disparate case studies and provides an informal literature recap, including some unrelated prevalence statistics and anecdotal recruitment experiences that are not part of the prespecified protocol or statistical plan.
documents.reasoning_trace: Provides domain background and tangential history; not used for answering the specific design and analysis questions.

task_row_model.golden_answer: The trial planned to enroll 240 participants randomized 1:1 to intervention or control. The primary outcome was change in clinic systolic blood pressure from baseline to 12 weeks, measured as the average of three seated automated readings per visit. The primary analysis specified ANCOVA adjusting for baseline systolic BP (and site) with a two-sided alpha of 0.05 following intention-to-treat.
